title: Should I Diagram the Passage or Write Notes?
transcript:
0:00
All right, you are about to see me display the greatest degree of flexibility that I will in this entire course. And so get ready.

0:06
Should you diagram or write any notes during the RC passage? Short answer, I don't really care, but I will tell you what to watch out for as you make your own decisions. And the reason why I don't really care,

0:18
the reason why I don't have like a super firm opinion on notes or markup of like highlight, underline, all of that kind of stuff is because in my experience, they don't really change the score at all.

0:28
It's, you know, you can do it if it really makes you feel better. But most of the impact is going to be psychological comfort of how it makes you feel. And you know, whether there's a time investment component to that, beyond that, the score doesn't really get affected whether you mark up or don't

0:46
mark up. And same thing with notes. The score doesn't really change whether you take notes or don't take notes.

1:09
just make sure that your Translation skills and especially your Translation recall are not dependent on those notes that you're taking.

For instance, I don't want you to be like, oh, well, I could remember the second paragraph if I read my notes on it.

isolation from a reliance on note taking. And so then one other thing about highlighting and underlining. So sometimes students will really overlook things like adjectives or certain modifier words or the word like only or whatever.

Then sometimes in a short term drill environment, I'll say, okay, for your next, let's say two or three sections, highlight all the adjectives or highlight all the only never always is or whatever it might be.

As long as it's not manifesting like that. And it's really just kind of like a mental note taking device of certain marks on the passage.

No problem with it whatsoever. You just need to make sure that you're not letting that technique become the star of the show to the point where you're focusing more on highlighting and underlining or note taking than you are the passage itself.
